mcqs.question: Consider the pair of linear equations 3x + 2y = 5 and 6x + 4y = 10. Which statement correctly identifies the nature of its solution?

options.A: The system has a unique solution because the coefficients of x and y are different.
options.B: The system has infinitely many solutions because the second equation is a multiple of the first.
options.C: The system has no solution because the constants are not proportional.
options.D: The system has a unique solution because its determinant is non‑zero.

mcqs.answer: The system has infinitely many solutions because the second equation is a multiple of the first.
mcqs.explanation: The second equation (6x + 4y = 10) is exactly twice the first (3x + 2y = 5). Hence both equations represent the same straight line, giving infinitely many common points. Option A is a common misconception that different coefficients guarantee a unique solution, which is false when the equations are proportional. Options C and D are incorrect for the same reason.

mcqs.question: Which of the following systems of two linear equations has infinitely many solutions?
mcqs.explanation: In option A the second equation is exactly twice the first, so both represent the same line and the system has infinitely many solutions. Option B has non‑proportional constants, leading to parallel lines (no solution). Option C also represents the same line (infinitely many), but only one correct answer is required; option A was chosen. Option D has different constant terms, giving parallel distinct lines (no solution).

mcqs.question: Four pairs of linear equations are given below. Which pair has no solution?
mcqs.explanation: In option B the second equation is not a multiple of the first (the left‑hand sides are proportional but the constants are not), so the two lines are parallel and never intersect, giving no solution. Options A, C, and D each consist of equations that are exact multiples of each other, representing the same line and therefore having infinitely many solutions.

mcqs.learning_point: Use coefficient relationships to classify a pair
mcqs.question: For the system a₁x + b₁y = c₁ and a₂x + b₂y = c₂, which condition guarantees that the system is inconsistent (has no solution)?
mcqs.explanation: When the ratios of the coefficients of x and y are equal but the ratio of the constants differs, the two equations represent parallel distinct lines, leading to no point of intersection—hence an inconsistent system. Option B describes coincident lines (infinitely many solutions). Option C indicates the lines intersect at a single point (unique solution). Option D is not a valid linear system.

mcqs.question: In the context of a pair of linear equations in two variables, a 'consistent system' is one that:

options.D: has at least one solution (either a unique solution or infinitely many solutions).

mcqs.answer: has at least one solution (either a unique solution or infinitely many solutions).
mcqs.explanation: A consistent system is defined as a system that possesses at least one solution. This includes both the case of a single intersection point (unique solution) and the case where the two equations represent the same line (infinitely many solutions). Options A and C describe only part of the possibilities, while B describes an inconsistent system.

mcqs.question: An 'inconsistent system' of two linear equations in two variables means:

options.A: the equations represent the same straight line.
options.B: the equations represent two parallel distinct lines.
options.C: the equations intersect at exactly one point.
options.D: the equations have infinitely many common solutions.

mcqs.answer: the equations represent two parallel distinct lines.
mcqs.explanation: When two linear equations are inconsistent, their graphs are parallel lines that never meet, so there is no common solution. Option A describes coincident lines (consistent with infinite solutions). Option C describes a unique solution (consistent). Option D also describes a consistent system.

mcqs.question: Which statement correctly distinguishes a system with a unique solution from one with infinitely many solutions?

options.A: Unique solution occurs when a₁/a₂ = b₁/b₂ = c₁/c₂; infinite solutions occur when a₁/a₂ ≠ b₁/b₂.
options.B: Unique solution occurs when a₁/a₂ ≠ b₁/b₂; infinite solutions occur when a₁/a₂ = b₁/b₂ = c₁/c₂.
options.C: Unique solution occurs when both equations are identical; infinite solutions occur when the equations are parallel.
options.D: Unique solution occurs when the determinant is zero; infinite solutions occur when the determinant is non‑zero.

mcqs.answer: Unique solution occurs when a₁/a₂ ≠ b₁/b₂; infinite solutions occur when a₁/a₂ = b₁/b₂ = c₁/c₂.
mcqs.explanation: If the ratios of the coefficients of x and y are different (a₁/a₂ ≠ b₁/b₂), the lines intersect at exactly one point, giving a unique solution. If the ratios of both coefficients and constants are equal (a₁/a₂ = b₁/b₂ = c₁/c₂), the equations represent the same line, leading to infinitely many solutions. Options A, C, and D invert or misstate these conditions.

mcqs.question: A student writes the equations 5x - 3y = 10 and 10x - 6y = 20. What can be concluded about the solution set of this system?

options.B: The system has exactly one solution.
options.C: The system has infinitely many solutions.
options.D: The nature of the solution cannot be determined from the given information.

mcqs.answer: The system has infinitely many solutions.
mcqs.explanation: The second equation is exactly twice the first (10x - 6y = 20 is 2 × (5x - 3y = 10)). Hence both equations describe the same straight line, so every point on that line satisfies both equations, giving infinitely many solutions. Options A and B are therefore incorrect, and D is unnecessary because the relationship is clear.
